notes:
Read the whole file (351 lines) and the feature delta (git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9). Delta touches exactly three spots: (1) sign_up_params (line 310) now permits :utm_source, :utm_campaign, :internal_ref as scalars and utm_data: {} as the trailing arbitrary-key hash-permit; (2) magic_create's user_params merges the four fields into BOTH conditional branches (connect branch lines 97-100, else branch lines 110-113); (3) #create is unchanged in body — it threads the four via sign_up_params.merge -> build_resource (lines 13-20). Chain traced: registrations_controller.rb -> user.rb (columns/enums/from_omniauth analog) -> db/schema.rb (users table) -> questions_controller.rb:50 (utm_data:{} analog).

MASS-ASSIGNMENT SAFETY: All four map to real users columns (db/schema.rb:1285-1288: utm_source string, utm_campaign string, utm_data jsonb, internal_ref string). None is an enum or has a custom accessor (only partner_source, role, sign_on_provider are enums; utm/internal_ref are plain columns), so direct mass-assignment via build_resource is safe and cannot raise. utm_data: {} is the documented arbitrary-hash permit and matches the blessed analog questions_controller.rb:50 (options: {} -> questions.options jsonb), which proves ActionController::Parameters -> jsonb assignment works in this app. No privilege-escalating attribute is exposed by the added permits.

KEY COLLISIONS: No overlaps. #create: sign_up_params keys (name/first_name/last_name/email/password/beta_token/registration_stripe_plan/referral/partner/organization_slug/login_intent/utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref/utm_data) merged with {created_via, partner_source} — disjoint. magic_create connect branch: base {email, partner_source} merged with {created_via, password, password_confirmation, connect_login_intent_organization_id, utm_source, utm_campaign, utm_data, internal_ref} — disjoint. else branch: base {email, partner_source} merged with {created_via, password, password_confirmation, utm_*, internal_ref} — disjoint. The four utm keys never shadow or get shadowed.

GUARD ORDERING: #create has no guard between entry and build_resource that rejects utm-bearing requests (invite_token handling is post-save). magic_create runs the recaptcha guard first (returns on failure — applies uniformly to all requests, utm or not), then org lookup, then builds user_params; no guard singles out utm-bearing requests. Confirmed no guard drops the utm payload before persistence.

utm_data JSONB PERSISTENCE on BOTH paths: #create -> sign_up_params[:utm_data] (permitted nested params) rides sign_up_params into build_resource -> jsonb column. magic_create -> explicit utm_data: sign_up_params[:utm_data] in both branches -> build_resource(user_params) in the else branch -> jsonb column. Round-trips per the questions analog.

NIL/ABSENT HANDLING: No fabricated fallbacks. magic_create writes utm_*: sign_up_params[:key], which is nil when the param is absent — nil is the natural absent value, no || '' / || {} substitution; spec §4.2 and Risk 256 require exactly this (absent -> column nil, utm_data nil not {}). #create only includes a key when strong-params found it present. Matches from_omniauth (user.rb:389-392), which likewise assigns the raw value with no fallback.

EXISTING-USER BRANCHES UNTOUCHED: magic_create's two existing-user branches (line 119 confirmed user -> magic-link generation; line 146 unconfirmed user -> resend confirmation) never call build_resource and read only user_params[:email]; attribution columns on existing Users are never written. Only the new-user else branch (build_resource + resource.save) creates a row, so values land only at creation. Matches spec Note 256 (creation-time only, existing logins never updated).

STRUCTURAL COMPARISON vs from_omniauth analog (user.rb:379-397): the SSO path assigns utm_source/utm_campaign/utm_data/internal_ref raw inside the first_or_create block with no transformation (no downcase, no mapping) — identical raw-passthrough semantics to the controller's mass-assignment. Consistent. partner_source keeps its &.downcase in both, created_via keeps its get_created_via mapping in both — the utm fields correctly do NOT get the enum/mapping treatment that partner_source/created_via get.

SETTLED (not re-flagged): M2 connect-branch organization.id-on-nil crash makes the connect-branch utm keys dormant — the else branch handles all live signups incl. connect-with-org, so utm is not lost for real connect signups. M1/M3 (SSO session tracking) out of this file.

ONE NEUTRAL PRE-EXISTING OBSERVATION (not a feature finding, unrelated to attribution): partner_source is an enum with only {none:0, wwr:1} (user.rb:57-60) yet both #create (line 15) and magic_create assign partner_source: params[:partner]&.downcase; get_created_via maps partner values 'weworkremotely'/'producthunt'/'connect' — any of those would raise ArgumentError on the enum setter. Pre-existing, untouched by this feature, and triggerability depends on frontend-controlled partner values I cannot verify; noted, not flagged.
